top_strength: The intake structure was genuinely good and she opened with a real agenda statement, which almost nobody does: 'I'll ask you some questions and then prepare the estimate... I'll send everything via email. This may take five to ten minutes. Sounds good.' Her box-count technique was the best moment on the call — she anchored with a benchmark first ('for a house the size we would typically see around 45 to 55 boxes') and then narrowed to a real number, which is exactly how to get an honest answer. She also caught and corrected the customer's policy error live: when Brian asked 'is it a two hour minimum?' she came back with 'two and a half hour minimum' rather than letting it slide. And she was patient and unhurried while he hunted for his new address — 'Sure, take your time' and 'Take your time. No worries.'
coaching_note: Amy, the highest-leverage fix is that you priced this move without ever selling it. Brian told you exactly what he needed — 'I'm just seeing if we're going to be able to afford it, they've gotten some quotes before and they're pretty high' — and the next thing out of your mouth was a rate number. That is a value conversation, not a math conversation. It should have sounded like: 'Pricing is super simple — $206 an hour on Friday, and that includes the truck, gas, taxes, insurance, all the wrap and pads and tools, and we disassemble and reassemble your furniture at no charge. There's no credit card fee, no transportation fee, no fuel surcharge. You also get our No Worries Damage Coverage, up to $2,000 per move, and there's no deposit — you don't pay anything today to hold the date.' Those cost you 14 points in Section 3 alone and they are the reason the call ended with 'it's a little so high' instead of a booking. Second priority: you never asked for the business. You confirmed you had trucks open on the 11th and then said 'shop on tomorrow' — never once 'we have availability, want me to lock that in? There's no deposit, so nothing to lose.' Third, and this is the part that worries me most: LIVE BUSINESS RISK — you quoted the 2.5-hour minimum ($515 Friday / $480 Mon–Thu) as though it were the price of the move. A two-story 1,100–1,200 sqft townhome with a washer/dryer, a 93-inch couch, roughly 20 boxes and one straight flight of 30 stairs at the destination is not a 2.5-hour job, and you never gave him a time range or a mover count. He is now shopping competitors against a number we cannot hit, and if he ever books he gets a day-of surprise. Always land the estimate: hours range, movers, trucks, and what would push it up or down. One more flag for review: the transcript records you saying '$206 minus $19,214 per hour' when explaining the weekday savings — likely a transcription garble of '$14', but worth an audio check to be sure he heard the discount correctly.
phone_presence_notes: Polite and patient in spots ('take your time, no worries') but largely transactional, with several confused or misfiring interjections and no acknowledgment of the customer's stated money anxiety before the call was closed out.
audio_review_reason: Transcript is noticeably garbled through the pricing segment ('$19,214 per hour', '$2 Hu', 'I'm start moving') — need audio to confirm what the customer actually heard about the weekday discount and the minimum, and to verify tone at the price objection.
